- Clinical morphology: 2 cm, dome-shaped, firm, non-tender, well-demarcated plaque with central keratin plug on sun-damaged forehead — classic presentation of hypertrophic actinic keratosis.  
- Histopathology reports *“minimal keratinocyte atypia”* — the defining histologic feature of actinic keratosis (particularly hypertrophic subtype), which typically shows variable but generally mild-to-moderate atypia confined to the epidermis.  
- The summary explicitly states the biopsy findings are *“most consistent with hypertrophic actinic keratosis”* — a direct, expert interpretation anchored in the available clinical and histologic data.  
- No immunosuppression or prior skin cancer — factors associated with lower risk of progression to SCC and supporting a diagnosis of AK over invasive malignancy.  

[GAPS]  
- The punch biopsy did not assess invasion beyond the basement membrane — critical for excluding invasive squamous cell carcinoma.  
- Depth of atypia (epidermal only vs. extending into dermis) was not determined — needed to distinguish AK from SCC *in situ* or invasive SCC.  
- Architectural maturation (e.g., differentiation gradient, polarity) was not evaluated — key for distinguishing benign/hyperplastic changes from dysplasia.  
- Margins were not assessed — relevant for determining field cancerization or residual disease, especially in a 2 cm lesion.  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Hypertrophic actinic keratosis
